title: Expression Analysis of Selected miRNAs in COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Modulations in microRNA (miRNA) expression can contribute to disease pathogenesis and biological processes by regulating target proteins. We aimed to compare serum miRNA levels (miR-19a-3p, miR-19b-3p, miR-21, miR-26a-5p, miR-146a, let-7b-3p, miR-155, miR-16, miR-590, miR-1307-3p) between COVID-19 patients and healthy controls to investigate their clinical significance and contribution to disease pathogenesis. Blood samples were obtained from 70 patients diagnosed with COVID-19 and from 30 healthy individuals as a control group for comparison. The patients were stratified into three categories based on disease severity: mild, moderate, and severe. miRNA expression levels were quantified via real-time PCR, with relative quantification performed using the Livak ΔΔCT method by calculating the 2(−ΔΔCT) fold change values. In patients with COVID-19, the expression levels of miR-1307-3p, miR-146, miR-26a-5p, miR-21, miR-19b-3p, and let-7b-3p demonstrated statistically significant differences (p < 0.05). A non-significant downward trend of miR-16 was observed, with miRNA expression profiles exhibiting variability across the different patient groups. Considering host–virus interactions, we posit that miRNAs hold significant potential both as novel therapeutic targets and as pivotal regulators in deciphering the intricate pathogenesis of COVID-19. Comprehensive elucidation of disease pathogenesis requires the synergistic integration of in vivo and in vitro experimental approaches in conjunction with rigorous clinical investigations.

title: Chimeric SARS-CoV-2 vaccine vectors stably incorporating the functional glycoprotein of VSV
abstract: Respiratory viruses, such as SARS-CoV-2, remain a global medical challenge, highlighting the need for adaptable vaccine platforms that elicit broad immunity while allowing flexible antigen design. Building on our established envelope-deleted (ΔE) SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate, we engineered chimeric variants that stably express the glycoprotein of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV-G) as a model antigen, with or without co-expression of the native SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Both constructs were genetically stable and displayed functional VSV-G, as shown by expanded, ACE2-independent tropism. Cryo-electron microscopy confirmed the presence of heterologous glycoproteins on virions. In vivo , both chimeric viruses exhibited an excellent safety profile and induced antigen-specific humoral responses against the encoded glycoproteins in Syrian hamsters and K18-hACE2 mice. Together, these findings demonstrate stable genetic incorporation and display of a functional heterologous glycoprotein into a SARS-CoV-2 virion, supporting use of the ΔE SARS-CoV-2 backbone as a potential platform for viral vector engineering and heterologous antigen delivery.

title: COVID-19 and Appendicitis: Insights from a Retrospective Study
abstract: To identify whether a relationship exists between COVID-19 and appendicitis and compare the incidence of appendicitis during three pandemic years to the year prior to the pandemic, we conducted two observational retrospective studies: a propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort and a repeated monthly cross-sectional study. We used data from the Military Health System (MHS) Data Repository, which contains data about healthcare provided to active-duty service members, retirees, and their dependents. For the PSM cohort of 753,138 individuals, patients with COVID-19 between July 2020 and June 2021 from the MHS were matched to two similar people without COVID-19. Survival analysis using a conditional Cox proportional hazards model explored these relationships. For the cross-sectional study we used a separate, unmatched MHS cohort of 10,402,021 individuals. Poisson regression generated incident rate ratios (IRRs) of any appendicitis or complicated appendicitis by year, comparing three pandemic years to one pre-pandemic year. COVID-19 was associated with appendicitis or appendectomy within the first year of infection (hazard ratio: 1.13, 95% confidence interval: 1.02–1.26). The IRRs for both any appendicitis and complicated appendicitis were significantly less than one when comparing individual pandemic years to the pre-pandemic year. COVID-19 is associated with appendicitis. Rates of any appendicitis and complicated appendicitis were lower in each individual pandemic year.

title: Neurological Manifestations of Long COVID: Current Evidence, Emerging Concepts, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Six years after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, many individuals continue to experience persistent neurological symptoms that extend beyond the acute phase of infection, affecting daily life, work, and overall functioning, thereby representing a substantial long-term health burden. Cognitive impairment, fatigue, headache, and autonomic dysfunction are among the most frequently reported neurological features, often persisting despite the absence of clear diagnostic findings. Although Long COVID is recognized as a distinct clinical entity, the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This narrative review provides a critical synthesis of current literature regarding the clinical presentations, potential mechanisms, and biomarkers associated with neurological involvement in Long COVID. Reflecting the high heterogeneity of the available evidence, it is important to note that no neurological biomarker or disease-modifying therapy has yet been clinically validated. Ultimately, characterizing these pathways may help define disease heterogeneity, support patient stratification, and guide future personalized therapeutic approaches.

title: The accessory protein ORF3a hijacks the CLCC1 chloride channel to disrupt ER homeostasis in betacoronavirus pathogenesis
abstract: Abstract Beta-coronavirus infection disrupts endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis; however, the mechanisms by which viral proteins manipulate ER-resident factors remain unclear. Here, we report that the SARS-CoV-2 accessory protein ORF3a binds to the ER chloride channel CLCC1, thereby impairing ER ion homeostasis, activating the unfolded protein response, and inducing endomembrane remodeling. Using newly developed ratiometric reporters, we showed that this interaction exacerbated the basal levels of ER-phagy and nucleophagy. Importantly, CLCC1 counteracted ORF3a by sequestering it within the ER, attenuating its toxicity and suppressing viral replication, which established CLCC1 as a host restriction factor. We further elucidated a spatiotemporal mechanism: during early infection, ORF3a accumulates in the ER, co-assembles with CLCC1 into puncta, and disrupts ER homeostasis; at the later stage, ORF3a overload enables its escape from CLCC1-mediated ER retention and subsequent translocation to lysosomes, facilitating viral egress. This ER-centric function is conserved across diverse beta-coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-1 and bat- or pangolin-derived strains, revealing a unified pathogenic strategy. Furthermore, in mouse brains, the ORF3a-CLCC1 axis recapitulates key neuropathological features, including ER stress, autophagic dysfunction, neuronal death, and neuroinflammation, providing a mechanistic link to COVID-19-associated neurological symptoms. Our findings identify CLCC1 as an essential host defense protein and establish a conceptual framework to guide future research on antiviral responses at the organelle level and related disease mechanisms.

title: Mental disorders, service use, and perceived treatment need among college students after the COVID-19 pandemic and the role of social connection: an epidemiological study
abstract: College students affected by mental disorders can be very impaired; yet, treatment rates remain low. The COVID-19 pandemic undoubtably posed strain on students, limiting their social life, which is an important determinant of health. However, recent estimates of mental health problems and service use are lacking and the understanding of the association between social connection and mental health and service use is limited. Cross-sectional data from the Flemish College Surveys conducted in 2022–2023 were used to estimate the 12-month prevalence of six common mental disorders (major depressive episode, general anxiety disorder, panic disorder, (hypo)mania, alcohol use disorder, and substance use disorder), suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STBs), functional impairment, social connection, service use and perceived need for treatment. A total of 21,313 students completed the surveys. Our results show that mental disorders remain highly prevalent, with 57% of students suffering from any disorder or STB, with substantial variations in functional impairment. Service use remains low (42% with any disorder or STB), and many students perceive an unmet need for treatment (33% with any disorder or STB). Although most students have a social network, 34% often feel lonely, and almost 6% has no one to confide in. Social connection reduced the odds of any mental disorder or STB and increased the odds of service use and perceived unmet need. Social connection might be a valuable protective factor for mental health among college students, both in reducing the odds for mental disorders as in increasing the odds for service use.

title: Predictors of survival among hospitalized COVID-19 patients in the Gambia, 2020–2022
abstract: In The Gambia, in-hospital mortality among laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients rose markedly, from 28.2% in 2020 to 48.4% in 2022. This mortality metric reflects proportion of deaths among admitted patients, distinct from the population-level case-fatality rate. Evidence on predictors of survival among hospitalised patients remains limited. We aimed to estimate in-hospital survival probability and identify independent predictors of time to death among COVID-19 patients admitted in The Gambia from March 2020 to December 2022. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 705 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients admitted to Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital and the Medical Research Council Clinic. The primary outcome was time (days) to in-hospital death, with medical discharge as a competing event and admission date as time origin. Fine-Gray competing-risks regression estimated sub-distribution hazard ratios (SHRs) for mortality (95% CI; p < 0.05). Sensitivity analyses assessed the impact of excluding patients discharged against medical advice. Overall, in-hospital mortality was 33.3% (235/705), with an incidence rate of 40.1 deaths per 1,000 person-days. Most deaths occurred within the first 21 days. Advanced age was the strongest predictor (adjusted SHR: 3.54 for 50–59 years; 6.96 for ≥ 70 years). Independent comorbidities included chronic liver disease (SHR 3.20), cardiac failure (SHR 2.15), chronic kidney disease (SHR 1.91), and diabetes mellitus (SHR 1.78). Prospective studies with standardised clinical data are needed to refine mortality prediction in this setting.

source_records.abstract: In The Gambia, in-hospital mortality among laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients rose markedly, from 28.2% in 2020 to 48.4% in 2022. title: Immune correlates analysis of the mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine efficacy clinical trial
abstract: In the coronavirus efficacy (COVE) phase 3 clinical trial, vaccine recipients were assessed for neutralizing and binding antibodies as correlates of risk for COVID-19 disease and as correlates of protection. These immune markers were measured at the time of second vaccination and 4 weeks later, with values reported in standardized World Health Organization international units. All markers were inversely associated with COVID-19 risk and directly associated with vaccine efficacy. Vaccine recipients with postvaccination 50% neutralization titers 10, 100, and 1000 had estimated vaccine efficacies of 78% (95% confidence interval, 54 to 89%), 91% (87 to 94%), and 96% (94 to 98%), respectively. These results help define immune marker correlates of protection and may guide approval decisions for messenger RNA (mRNA) COVID-19 vaccines and other COVID-19 vaccines.
authors: Coronavirus Vaccine Prevention Network (CoVPN)/Coronavirus Efficacy (COVE) Team

title: On a new model of COVID-19 transmission by incorporating booster dose vaccination and suggested treatments in India
abstract: In this study, a COVID-19 model that is driven by an eight-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations is developed and analyzed, incorporating the primary and booster dose vaccinated individual’s compartments. Initially, the basic properties of the model are examined, and the threshold quantity is obtained. Further, the stability of the equilibrium points of the model is investigated analytically. Moreover, a nonlinear least squares technique is used to calibrate the model parameters based on the cumulative number of COVID-19 reported cases in India. The best-fitted model parameters are found to interpret the consequences of various parameters. In addition, sensitivity analysis is investigated and awareness parameter is identified as the most influential parameter. Moreover, a numerical simulation of the model has been done to compare the consequences of vaccination. In addition, the essence of vaccine efficacy and awareness are examined by considering the different scenarios. It has been found that perceiving preventive measures (pharmaceutical or non-pharmaceutical) significantly reduces the spread of disease amongst the people. Particularly, an increment in the booster dose vaccination and awareness of the disease reduces the number of infected individuals and expands the recovery. Therefore, it is instructed that to protect India from another outbreak of COVID-19, the speed of the booster dose vaccination and awareness campaign should be encouraged.

title: Changes in gluten-free diet adherence and growth parameters among children with celiac disease during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Strict exclusion of gluten is the cornerstone of celiac disease (CD) management; nevertheless, maintaining dietary adherence remains challenging. The COVID-19 pandemic may have influenced dietary adherence in children with CD. This study aimed to investigate the association between the COVID-19 pandemic and gluten-free diet (GFD) adherence and anthropometric measurements. This retrospective longitudinal cohort study with a cross-sectional survey component included 81 pediatric patients with CD (67.9% female; mean age 14.9 ± 3.4 years) who had been following a GFD for at least one year before the pandemic. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, and anthropometric data from the pre-pandemic, restriction, and post-pandemic periods were obtained from medical records. Dietary adherence was assessed via a structured telephone questionnaire. Participants reporting either complete avoidance of gluten or fewer than six inadvertent gluten exposures annually were categorized as self-reported adherent. Serological adherence was defined by a negative tTG-IgA result. At the beginning of the pandemic in March 2020, the mean duration of GFD was 3.9 ± 2.4 years. At the time of the survey, self-reported adherence was 67.9% (55/81), whereas serological adherence was 77.1% (54/70). During the pandemic, 49.4% of participants reported no change in dietary adherence, 33.3% reported increased adherence, and 17.3% reported decreased adherence. Serological adherence differed significantly across the three longitudinal assessment periods (Cochran's Q = 31.818, p < 0.001). Compared with the pre-pandemic period (51.9%, 42/81), serological adherence was significantly higher during both the restriction period (82.7%, 67/81) and the post-pandemic period (76.5%, 62/81) (McNemar p < 0.001 for both comparisons), whereas no significant difference was observed between the restriction and post-pandemic periods (McNemar p = 0.227). Serological adherence was associated with home-cooking and selected family and socioeconomic factors. Most participants (87.7%) reported difficulty accessing gluten-free products, mainly due to high cost and limited variety. No significant differences were observed in anthropometric measurements across the study periods. Serological adherence was significantly higher during both the COVID-19 restriction and post-pandemic periods than during the pre-pandemic period, while no significant changes in anthropometric measurements were observed.

title: Effects of conspiracy beliefs, trust in government, and perceived government response on COVID-19 vaccination in European countries.
abstract: AIMS Although the effects of conspiracy beliefs and trust in government on COVID-19 vaccination behavior have been analyzed in numerous studies, the interrelationships between these factors and the mechanisms through which they influence vaccination behavior remain underexplored. We hypothesized that conspiracy beliefs are negatively associated with trust in government, which is subsequently and positively associated with attitudes toward and satisfaction with government response, ultimately affecting vaccination behavior. METHODS For this cross-sectional multilevel study, data were collected from the 10th round (2022) of the European Social Survey. Participants from 18 countries who completed the COVID-19 module of this survey were included in the analysis (N = 27,983). Data were analyzed using a two-step approach, combining generalized linear mixed models with random intercept and structural equation models. RESULTS Conspiracy beliefs were negatively associated with trust in government (β = -0.506). Furthermore, conspiracy beliefs (β = -0.125) and trust in government (β = 0.150) were negatively and positively associated with vaccination intention and behavior respectively. Both factors indirectly affected vaccination behavior through individuals' satisfaction with COVID-19 interventions and attitudes toward government response. Attitudes were more strongly associated with conspiracy beliefs (β = -0.237), whereas satisfaction was more strongly associated with trust in government (β = 0.509). CONCLUSIONS Our study demonstrated the complex interrelationships among conspiracy beliefs, trust in government, and COVID-19 vaccination. Policymakers should invest in transparent, evidence-based communication strategies to counter misinformation during public health crises.

title: A contextual framework for bibliometric integrity: synthesizing positivist and rationalist paradigms in the analysis of African LIS research during COVID-19
abstract: This paper aims to examines bibliometric analysis’s role in advancing academic integrity through contextual citation practices. It identifies methodological and conceptual gaps in the literature. The paper proposes a philosophically informed novel framework integrating positivist and rationalist paradigms to address these limitations. A multi-phase mixed-methods design is employed, combining a comprehensive literature review, a diagnostic critique of a prior study, and an illustrative case study. The empirical component reanalyses COVID-19’s impact on African Library and Information Science research via triangulated data from Scopus, Google Scholar, journal metadata and author surveys. The diagnostic critique identifies common shortcomings: temporal oversimplification, contextual blindness, data source bias and overreliance on descriptive statistics. The case study demonstrates that applying the contextual framework yields more nuanced insights. Key results show preexisting publishing infrastructure, not the pandemic, primarily drove output, and citation visibility varied significantly across databases. While the illustrative case study validates the framework’s utility, broader application across diverse geographic and disciplinary contexts is needed. Future research should test and refine the framework in varied settings to establish its generalizability. Researchers should adopt context-sensitive bibliometric practices, including mixed-methods designs, data source triangulation, and consideration of local scholarly infrastructures to support more equitable and credible research assessment, particularly for underrepresented regions. This paper provides a novel, philosophically grounded framework synthesizing positivist and rationalist traditions. It offers a critical diagnostic tool and a constructive methodological model, supported by original empirical evidence from an under-researched regional context.

title: Changes in positive mental health before and after the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated sociodemographic characteristics and COVID-19-related stressors
abstract: We aimed to examine the dynamic changes in positive mental health (PMH) over a period of 12 years between 2012 and 2024, and explore their relationships with sociodemographic characteristics, with additional exploratory analyses of COVID-19-related stressors with PMH in 2024. A total of 894 participants from an established longitudinal cohort with complete PMH before and after the outbreak of the pandemic were analyzed. Generalized linear mixed models and multivariate logistic regression were used to investigate the associations of changes in PMH with sociodemographic characteristics and COVID-19-related stressors. Flourishing PMH decreased from 57.9-62.8% to 49.1-52.4% before and after the pandemic. Changes in flourishing PMH were associated with age, marital status, occupation, and the interactions between age and occupation and age and marital status (P < 0.05). Furthermore, flourishing PMH in 2024 was also associated with employment stressors during the pandemic (P < 0.05). These findings demonstrate changes in flourishing PMH before and after the pandemic, and the inequality in PMH across these identified social determinants. This study suggests the need for comprehensive community mental health strategies that integrate individual, social, and contextual factors to cope with public emergencies like the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Resurgence and molecular epidemiology of dengue virus serotype 4 amid the COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Dengue virus serotype 4 (DENV4) co-circulates with other serotypes in Thailand, a hyperendemic setting characterized by cyclical shifts in serotype predominance. During the COVID-19 pandemic, related public health interventions may have influenced dengue detection, transmission and epidemiological dynamics. MATERIALS AND METHODS A total of 413 dengue NS1/PCR-positive samples collected from 2018 to 2024 at a tertiary hospital in Bangkok were serotyped using a real-time PCR DENV1-4 subtyping assay. Forty-seven DENV4-positive samples (Ct < 32) underwent whole-genome sequencing using the ATOPlex DENV1-4 panel on the DNBSEQ-G99RS platform. Sequencing reads were processed using CLC Genomics Workbench, followed by phylogenetic, mutation, codon-based selection-pressure, and epitope-mapping analyses. RESULTS DENV4 was identified in 18.2% (75/413) of samples, with 48% of cases requiring hospitalization. Detection increased markedly from 11.8% (22/186) during 2018-2021-23.3% (53/227) during 2022-2024 (proportion ratio, 1.97; p = 0.0025). Among the 47 whole-genome-sequenced samples, most strains clustered within genotype I lineage 4I_A.3 and showed lineage-associated non-synonymous substitutions. NS1-A90T, NS2A-L113F, and NS3-F523Y appeared exclusively during 2022-2024 (p < 0.001), whereas NS2A-L113F, NS5-G223S, and NS5-Q631R showed concordant positive-selection signals by FEL and MEME. CONCLUSIONS This hospital-based study highlights an increase in DENV4 detection in Bangkok during 2022-2024 compared with 2018-2021, accompanied by predominance of lineage 4I_A.3 distinct from Malaysian and Indonesian strains reported during a similar period. These findings support integrated clinical and genomic surveillance to monitor DENV serotype and genotype dynamics and inform public health and vaccine strategies.

title: Prognostic Factors Associated with Fatal Outcomes in COVID-19 Vaccine-Related Myocarditis
abstract: AIMS: Vaccine-related myocarditis (VRM) has gained attention during the global roll-out of COVID-19 vaccines. COVID-19 VRM is usually non-fatal, but factors associated with fatal outcomes remain unclear. We aimed to characterise features associated with reported fatal outcomes using a pharmacovigilance database. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed COVID-19 VRM reports in the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report database from 2021 to 2024. Reports were stratified into death and survival groups based on recorded outcome information. Logistic regression analyses identified factors associated with reported fatal outcomes. RESULTS: 31,022 reports listed COVID-19 vaccines as suspected drug; 1,041 reports included myocarditis (reporting odds ratio [ROR] 31.3, 95% CI 29.0-33.8). The median time from vaccination to myocarditis onset was 2 (1-4) days, with most events occurring within 7 days. Among reports with VRM, men accounted for the majority (77.8%) and 68.6% were ≤39 years old. Outcome data were available for 863 reports, and death was recorded in 97 reports (11.2% [95% CI, 9.3%-13.5%]). Reported fatal outcomes were more frequent in women, patients aged ≥70 years, those with delayed onset (≥8 days after COVID-19 vaccination), and those with ≥1 comorbidities. Multivariable logistic regression identified age ≥70 years as independently associated with reported fatal outcomes (OR 8.67, 95% CI 4.41-17.3; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Older age was associated with higher odds of reported fatal outcomes among VRM reports in JADER. Female sex, delayed onset, and comorbidities were more common among reports with fatal outcomes. These exploratory findings require validation in clinically adjudicated studies.

title: Impactos da cinesioterapia na fadiga muscular e na tolerância ao exercício em pacientes com síndrome pós-COVID-19: revisão sistematizada da literatura (2020–2026)
abstract: Post-COVID-19 syndrome is characterized by persistent clinical manifestations following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly muscle fatigue and exercise intolerance, which significantly impair functional capacity. This study aims to analyze the effects of kinesiotherapy on muscle fatigue and exercise tolerance in individuals with post-COVID-19 syndrome through a systematized literature review. A qualitative study was conducted using PubMed, SciELO, PEDro, and Google Scholar databases, considering publications from 2020 to 2026. Clinical studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses addressing therapeutic exercise interventions were included. The findings demonstrate that kinesiotherapy significantly improves peripheral muscle endurance, enhances cardiorespiratory capacity, and reduces perceived exertion. Improvements in functional performance and quality of life were also observed. Kinesiotherapy is therefore an effective intervention for post-COVID-19 rehabilitation when applied progressively and individually.
authors: Leane Do Socorro di Brito Morais

title: Early monocyte subset signatures predict outcomes in unvaccinated COVID-19 patients
abstract: Introduction Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection is characterized by complex immune responses, with monocytes playing a central role in disease pathogenesis. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the profiles of monocytes and their receptor expression during the first week of hospitalization in unvaccinated patients with COVID-19, stratified by clinical outcome: discharged or deceased. Methods Peripheral mononuclear cells from hospitalized patients were analyzed by flow cytometry to characterize classical, intermediate, and non-classical monocytes, along with the expression of CD169, CD209, and TLR2, TLR3, TLR4, and TLR9. Result Patients in whom death was the outcome exhibited a significant reduction in classical monocytes and an expansion of non-classical monocytes early during hospitalization. Additionally, non-classical monocytes from deceased patients showed increased expression of CD169 and greater intensity of CD209 expression. Enhanced expression of TLR2 across all monocyte subsets and increased TLR4 expression specifically in non-classical monocytes were also associated with mortality. Correlation network analysis revealed more complex and dysregulated interactions among monocyte subsets and immune markers in deceased patients compared with discharged individuals. Conclusion Our findings demonstrate that, during the first week of hospitalization, alterations in monocyte distribution and activation status are strongly associated with COVID-19 severity. Increased expression of CD169, CD209, TLR2, and TLR4, particularly in non-classical monocytes, reflects heightened innate immune activation and may contribute to poorer disease outcomes. Collectively, these results highlight the potential of monocyte subsets and their associated receptors as early prognostic biomarkers and provide insight into the immunopathogenesis of severe COVID-19.

title: Lessons Learnt from Using AI in COVID-19
abstract: Sometimes we conveniently choose not to dwell on the fact that health injustice, inequality, and inequity are prominent features within the health society and health system in the US, clearly demonstrated when the Black, Indigenous, and people of color (BIPOC) population endured a disproportionately high number of COVID-19 deaths. AI systems employed during the COVID-19 pandemic in the US showed substantial biases against Black and other minority populations. Preparations for future pandemics need to address AI biases against these minorities. Policymakers and researchers decided to use nontraditional data and AI-based methods for public health surveillance, informatics, and decision making because there were no reliable official statistics early in the pandemic, but this non-traditional data also produced strong ‘data mirages’ that reinforced health disparities. Early in the COVID-19 pandemic, some researchers held the view that one type of healthcare harm that was not subject to much legal scrutiny was algorithmic discrimination. Algorithmic discrimination could be in breach of US civil rights laws such as Title VI and Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act, as it worsens health disparities. While AI was transformative during COVID-19, such as fast-tracking vaccine discovery and diagnostics, it also played the role of a ‘force multiplier’ for health disparities. So, in any pandemic preparedness for the future, this question must be addressed: How can AI tools be employed to prevent deaths and reduce the socioeconomic costs of health crises globally?
journal: Ethics and Governance of AI in Healthcare

title: Integrating non-communicable disease screening to COVID-19 and human immunodeficiency virus care in Johannesburg South Africa: a pilot model for low- and middle-income countries
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the relationship between infectious diseases and non-communicable diseases (NCDs), highlighting increased risks for people with pre-existing chronic conditions. This study piloted an integrated care model for NCD and infectious disease screening in healthcare settings. The aim of this study is to show that integrating NCD screening into existing HIV clinics and COVID-19 vaccine delivery clinics leads to better pandemic preparedness. Methods From October 2023 to December 2023, we conducted a cross sectional prospective, low interventional study involving 461 participants from two health care clinics in Johannesburg, South Africa using convenience sampling. Screening included blood pressure, body mass index (BMI), HbA1c, lipid profile, glucose, and kidney function assessments. Data were analyzed to identify NCD prevalence and key risk factors. Results Newly diagnosed NCDs were found in 73.9% of participants. The most common were kidney disease (31.7%), obesity (28.9%), and dyslipidaemia (25.8%). Modifiable cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factors, including obesity (63.9%) and alcohol use (50%), were widespread. Conclusion Integrating NCD screening into HIV and COVID-19 services is achievable, offers a valuable opportunity for early detection and intervention. Scaling such models could strengthen health systems in resource-limited settings.

title: Counting the Costs of COVID-19: Why Future Treatment Option Values Matter
abstract: I critique a recent analysis (Miles, Stedman & Heald, 2020) of COVID-19 lockdown costs and benefits, focussing on the United Kingdom (UK). (2020) argue that the March-June UK lockdown was more costly than the benefit of lives saved, evaluated using the NICE threshold of £30000 for a quality-adjusted life year (QALY) and that the costs of a lockdown for 13 weeks from mid-June would be vastly greater than any plausible estimate of the benefits, even if easing produced a second infection wave causing over 7000 deaths weekly by mid-September. I note here two key problems that significantly affect their estimates and cast doubt on their conclusions. Firstly, their calculations arbitrarily cut off after 13 weeks, without costing the epidemic end state. That is, they assume indifference between mid-September states of 13 or 7500 weekly deaths and corresponding infection rates. This seems indefensible unless one assumes that (a) there is little chance of any effective vaccine or improved medical or social interventions for the foreseeable future, (b) notwithstanding temporary lockdowns, COVID-19 will very likely propagate until herd immunity. Even under these assumptions it is very questionable. Secondly, they ignore the costs of serious illness, possible long-term lowering of life quality and expectancy for survivors. These are uncertain, but plausibly at least as large as the costs in deaths.In summary, policy on tackling COVID-19 cannot be rationally made without estimating probabilities of future medical interventions and long-term illness costs. More work on modelling these uncertainties is urgently needed.

title: The Role of Positive Work Environments in Enhancing Employee Performance: Post-COVID-19 Myanmar’s Healthcare Sector
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed significant weaknesses in healthcare systems, particularly in maintaining employee performance under conditions of heightened uncertainty, psychological stress, and workforce shortages. In Myanmar, these challenges were intensified by resource constraints and institutional instability, highlighting the need to better understand workplace factors that sustain employee performance. This conceptual paper examines the influence of bonuses, recognition, and job security on healthcare employee performance during the COVID-19 pandemic through the lens of Herzberg’s Motivation–Hygiene Theory. The study adopts a conceptual review approach by synthesizing existing literature and contextual evidence to develop a theoretical framework linking motivational and hygiene factors with employee performance in Myanmar’s healthcare sector. The proposed framework identifies bonuses and recognition as key motivational factors that enhance employee engagement, commitment, and productivity, while job security functions as a hygiene factor that reduces dissatisfaction, strengthens psychological stability, and supports sustained performance. Based on the reviewed literature, three propositions are advanced, suggesting positive relationships between bonuses, recognition, job security, and employee performance. The framework further indicates that recognition is likely to exert the strongest influence on performance, with bonuses reinforcing organizational commitment and job security providing a supportive foundation for workforce resilience. This study contributes to the literature by extending Herzberg’s Motivation–Hygiene Theory to a crisis-affected healthcare context and offers a conceptual framework to guide future empirical research. The findings also provide practical insights for healthcare administrators and policymakers seeking to strengthen employee motivation, organizational resilience, and workforce performance during future public health emergencies.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Suicide-Related Emergency Department Presentations: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study from a Turkish Tertiary Care Center
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly affected mental health worldwide by increasing psychological distress, social isolation, unemployment, and barriers to healthcare access. These factors may have contributed to changes in suicidal behavior and emergency department (ED) utilization. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on suicide-related ED presentations in a tertiary care hospital in Türkiye. Methods This retrospective, cross-sectional study included adult patients (≥18 years) presenting to the emergency department with suicidal ideation or suicide attempts between March 11, 2019, and March 11, 2021. Eligible patients were identified using ICD-10 codes related to intentional self-harm. Demographic characteristics, employment status, marital status, suicide methods, psychiatric history, COVID-19 history, clinical outcomes, and healthcare costs were extracted from electronic medical records. Patients were divided into pre-pandemic (Group 1) and pandemic (Group 2) cohorts. Continuous and categorical variables were compared using appropriate statistical tests, with statistical significance defined as p < 0.05. Results A total of 750 patients were included, with a mean age of 32.27 ± 11.39 years. During the pandemic, suicide-related ED presentations increased from 0.125% to 0.264% of all ED visits despite a 39.4% reduction in overall emergency department admissions. The relative risk of suicide-related presentation during the pandemic was 2.11 (95% CI: 1.83–2.44; p < 0.001). The proportion of male patients increased significantly from 42.9% to 65.6% (p < 0.001), while unemployment and single marital status became more prevalent. Drug overdose remained the most common suicide method, although the use of more violent methods, including hanging and self-inflicted sharp object injuries, increased significantly (p = 0.017). Patients presenting during the pandemic were more frequently managed with short-term observation and less frequently required intensive care admission (p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in seasonal presentation patterns. Conclusions The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a marked increase in suicide-related emergency department presentations despite an overall decline in emergency department utilization. Significant changes in patient demographics, suicide methods, and clinical outcomes suggest that pandemic-related psychosocial stressors substantially influenced suicidal behavior. These findings emphasize the importance of maintaining accessible mental health services, implementing targeted suicide prevention strategies, and strengthening psychiatric support systems during future public health emergencies.

title: Effects of an outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program on exercise capacity, muscle fatigue, dyspnea, and functional status in post-COVID-19 patients: non-randomized clinical trial
abstract: Background COVID-19 may lead to persistent sequelae that impair functional capacity, resulting in dyspnea, fatigue, and limitations in activities of daily living. Objective To evaluate exercise capacity, fatigue, dyspnea, and functional status in patients following hospitalization for COVID-19 who underwent an outpatient pulmonary rehabilitation program (PRP). Methods The study was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of UniEVANGÉLICA (approval number 4,296,707; September 24, 2020) and registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT04982042). This prospective single-arm non-randomized clinical trial included symptomatic individuals after COVID-19 infection. Exercise capacity was assessed using the Six-Minute Walk Test, muscle fatigue using the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS), modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) Dyspnea Scale, and functional status using the Post-COVID-19 Functional Status Scale (PCFS). The PRP consisted of cardiorespiratory training and muscle strengthening exercises performed three times per week for six weeks. Results A total of 54 patients were included (29 in the Ward Group and 25 in the ICU Group). After the PRP, 6MWT distance increased from 428.52 ± 104.5 m to 503.19 ± 98.04 m ( p < 0.0001), mMRC dyspnea decreased from 3.50 ± 1.31 to 1.56 ± 0.60 ( p < 0.0001), PCFS improved from 2.91 ± 0.59 to 0.63 ± 0.75 ( p < 0.001), and FSS decreased from 4.68 ± 1.50 to 2.97 ± 1.55 ( p < 0.001). title: The Severity and Frequency of Self-Reported Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder Symptoms in Psychology University Students Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: This study measured the severity and frequency of self-reported symptoms of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in Psychology students in a Dutch university before and during the COVID-19 pandemic, providing insights into how this population navigated the challenges of emerging adulthood amidst a global crisis. In total, 1446 first-year Psychology students in a Dutch university were recruited in four cohorts: 2018 (n = 404), 2019 (n = 277), 2020 (n = 350), and 2021 (n = 415). The cohorts in 2020 and 2021 were recruited during the COVID-19 pandemic. Responses on the Conners’ Adult ADHD Rating Scale (CAARS) Long Form were collected. For each cohort, scale scores were calculated, as well as frequencies of students screening positive for elevated ADHD symptoms. The proportion of participants screening positive for elevated ADHD symptoms was 21%, which did not significantly differ between cohorts (p = 0.076) and gender (p = 0.206). Subscale scores were indicative of a small increase in inattention symptoms with increasing duration of the pandemic from cohort 2018 to 2021. Small gender differences were found on the subscales. Roughly one in five first-year Psychology students in university screens positive for elevated ADHD symptoms. This pattern is stable across men and women and across four cohorts of students before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. Inattention symptoms slightly increased with increasing duration of the pandemic in cohort 2021.

title: Parental attitudes toward routine childhood vaccination in the post-COVID-19 pandemic era
abstract: Abstract This study assessed parental attitudes toward routine childhood vaccination in five Arab countries (Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Libya) and explored factors associated with vaccine hesitancy in the post-coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic period. Using a cross-sectional design, 2095 parents or guardians of children aged ≤ 4 years were surveyed via online and face-to-face interviews. The Arabic version of the Parent Attitudes about Childhood Vaccines Scale was used to measure parental vaccine hesitancy. Overall, 18.8% of parents were classified as vaccine hesitant. In multivariable modified Poisson regression analysis, residing in Libya was associated with a significantly lower prevalence of vaccine hesitancy compared with Egypt (adjusted prevalence ratio (aPR): 0.14, 95% CI 0.07–0.28; p <0.001), whereas rural residence (aPR: 1.28, 95% CI 1.03–1.58; p = 0.024), unemployment (aPR: 1.26, 95% CI 1.01–1.56; p = 0.040), having a child born after the COVID-19 pandemic (aPR: 1.54, 95% CI 1.22–1.94; p <0.001), family history of COVID-19-related death (aPR: 1.34, 95% CI 1.08–1.65; p = 0.007), lack of parental COVID-19 vaccination (aPR: 1.56, 95% CI 1.26–1.92; p <0.001), and lower confidence in vaccinations provided by the health system (aPR: 2.24, 95% CI 1.77–2.83; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher parental vaccine hesitancy. Mediation analyses found no significant indirect associations through parental vaccine hesitancy on the relationships between education, country income, parental COVID-19 vaccination or infection history, and childhood vaccination. However, education, country income, and parental COVID-19 infection demonstrated significant direct effects on childhood vaccination status. These findings emphasize the importance of strengthening confidence in health systems and addressing socioeconomic disparities to reduce parental vaccine hesitancy and support childhood immunization programs in the post-pandemic era.

title: Integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analysis reveals a convergent cholangiocyte-associated host inflammatory program in biliary atresia and SARS-CoV-2-associated hepatobiliary injury
abstract: SARS-CoV-2-associated hepatobiliary injury and biliary atresia (BA) differ markedly in etiology and biological context, but both involve injury to the biliary epithelial compartment. Here, we performed integrative transcriptomic and single-cell analyses to investigate whether these distinct hepatobiliary injury contexts converge on a shared cholangiocyte-associated inflammatory host-response program. Bulk transcriptomic datasets from SARS-CoV-2-infected human liver organoids and BA liver tissues were integrated to identify shared transcriptional alterations, followed by functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction, regulatory network, drug-gene interaction, and molecular docking analyses. Single-nucleus and single-cell datasets were used to determine the cellular localization of the shared program, and key findings were further assessed in BA liver tissues and cultured human cholangiocytes exposed to poly(I:C). We identified an expanded exploratory set of 164 shared genes and a stringent FDR -adjusted core of 52 genes. Both sets consistently implicated antiviral defense, type I and type II interferon signaling, double-stranded RNA responses, and cytokine and chemokine signaling. STAT1, ISG15, and CXCL10 were retained in the stringent core and remained central components of the interaction network. In COVID-19 liver single-nucleus data, donor-level analysis showed preferential localization of the shared signature to cholangiocytes, whose mean scores were significantly higher than those of all other hepatic cells combined ( P = 0.00368). A similar pattern was observed descriptively in our BA single-nucleus dataset and further supported by an independent BA single-cell cohort. Tissue immunofluorescence spatially associated pSTAT1, total STAT1, and ISG15 signals with KRT19-positive ductular structures, whereas CXCL10 was predominantly periductal. Poly(I:C) stimulation induced representative components of the program in cultured cholangiocytes. Computational analyses retained mefloquine among the top-ranked exploratory candidates. Collectively, these findings support a convergent cholangiocyte-associated interferon/inflammatory host-response program in BA and SARS-CoV-2-associated hepatobiliary injury. They indicate molecular association rather than a common etiology or causal relationship and provide testable hypotheses for further investigation of biliary epithelial inflammatory responses.

title: The role of social media in enhancing health awareness, social support and educational progress among university students in Oman during the COVID-19 pandemic: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: This study examined the role of social media in promoting health awareness, strengthening social support, and maintaining educational continuity among university students during the early stage of the COVID-19 lockdown in Oman. It also explored the major challenges associated with social media use during this unprecedented public health emergency. A descriptive-analytical design was employed using an online survey administered to 380 undergraduate students at Sultan Qaboos University during the suspension of face-to-face teaching in April and May 2020. The findings indicate that social media played an important role in enhancing students’ awareness of COVID-19-related health issues, with a high overall awareness score (M = 40.92, SD = 5.47; relative strength = 85%). Students also reported substantial social benefits (M = 50.15, SD = 8.19; relative strength = 84%), particularly in strengthening social responsibility, maintaining communication with family and friends, and reducing the effects of social isolation. In addition, social media contributed positively to educational continuity during the lockdown (M = 30.80, SD = 7.89), especially by facilitating access to learning materials, communication with instructors, and the submission of assignments. Despite these benefits, students identified several important challenges (M = 34.02, SD = 5.67; relative strength = 77%), including the spread of misinformation and rumors, unreliable online content, high internet costs, and technical and connectivity problems. The findings highlight the value of social media as a complementary tool for health communication, social connectedness, and educational continuity during public health emergencies. They also provide insights that may inform digital communication strategies in higher education and public health campaigns. Although the study did not specifically investigate social work students or practitioners, the findings may also inform the development of digital competencies and electronic social work education for crisis preparedness. Further research should examine the role of social workers and social work education in emergencies and disaster contexts.

title: Pilot Monitoring of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in Influent and Treated Effluent of Municipal Wastewater Treatment Plants Across Slovakia During the Autumn 2020 COVID-19 Wave
abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance can track community SARS-CoV-2, but RNA signals at wastewater treatment plants are affected by sampling, analytical recovery and transfer to solids. We quantified SARS-CoV-2 RNA in influent and biologically treated effluent from eight Slovak municipal wastewater treatment plants during the period October–December 2020. Twenty-seven 24 h influent composites and seven same-day effluent samples were analysed by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR targeting ORF1b, S, E and RdRp. RNA was detected in 20/27 influents (74%; 95% CI, 54–89%) and 3/7 effluents (43%; 95% CI, 10–82%). Influent loads ranged from 4.66 × 109 to 5.60 × 1013 copies day−1; the maximum population-normalised load was 5.84 × 105 copies per population equivalent per day. All seven effluent concentrations were lower than paired influents (exact sign test, p = 0.0156). Apparent log10 reductions were 0.18 and 0.76 for quantifiable effluents, approximately 1.75 for one detection at the operational limit of detection, and ≥1.9–≥2.5 for four non-detects. A one-day process profile at the selected plant detected RNA in activated-sludge supernatant, digested-sludge supernatant and reject water. Because solids, infectivity and whole-process recovery were not measured, the results describe RNA occurrence rather than viral inactivation or a mass balance. These pilot data provide a historical baseline for Slovakia and define requirements for repeated sampling, process controls and paired liquid-solid measurements.

title: Macroeconomic rare disasters and lost decades in Latin America: the COVID-19 experience in a historical context
abstract: Abstract COVID-19 led to the single largest year-over-year decline in Latin America’s GDP per capita in more than a century. Although the region has endured several macroeconomic shocks before, mostly related to financial dislocations, none has been so deep and synchronized, as measured by the negative co-movement of GDP rates in the major regional economies. Our analysis of the COVID-19 experience for the region and eight economies with available historical data reveals the extent of the damage. Through 2020, four economies suffered “rare disasters” (cumulative contractions by 10% or more): Argentina, Mexico, Peru, and Venezuela. In addition, Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, and Venezuela, together with the Latin America regional aggregate, underwent a “lost decade” (prolonged periods of stagnation), which highlights the confluence of the large COVID-19 shock and scarring effects with the underlying vulnerabilities that in many cases were built over several decades.
journal: Revista de Historia Económica / Journal of Iberian and Latin American Economic History

source_records.title: Macroeconomic rare disasters and lost decades in Latin America: the COVID-19 experience in a historical context
source_records.abstract: Abstract COVID-19 led to the single largest year-over-year decline in Latin America’s GDP per capita in more than a century. Although the region has endured several macroeconomic shocks before, mostly related to financial dislocations, none has been so deep and synchronized, as measured by the negative co-movement of GDP rates in the major regional economies. Our analysis of the COVID-19 experience for the region and eight economies with available historical data reveals the extent of the damage. Through 2020, four economies suffered “rare disasters” (cumulative contractions by 10% or more): Argentina, Mexico, Peru, and Venezuela. In addition, Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, and Venezuela, together with the Latin America regional aggregate, underwent a “lost decade” (prolonged periods of stagnation), which highlights the confluence of the large COVID-19 shock and scarring effects with the underlying vulnerabilities that in many cases were built over several decades.

title: PERSISTENCE AND RECOVERY OF CHANGES IN WEIGHT STATUS ASSOCIATED WITH THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC AMONG CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS: A SYSTEMATICALLY INFORMED NARRATIVE REVIEW
abstract: Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted schooling, physical activity, diet, and daily routines, contributing to excess weight gain among children and adolescents. Whether these changes persisted after restrictions eased remains uncertain. Objectives: To evaluate the persistence of pandemic-associated changes in weight status among children and adolescents after major restrictions were eased. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through December 2025 for observational studies of general pediatric populations (<18 years) reporting weight-related outcomes before the pandemic, during lockdown, school closure, or other major restrictions, and at least six months after school reopening or restriction easing. Owing to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis. Results: Ten studies from nine countries were included. Most reported increases in BMI-related measures or the prevalence of overweight or obesity during the pandemic or restriction period. After restrictions eased, adverse trends generally attenuated, but complete normalization was inconsistent. Recovery was more frequently observed among younger children, whereas residual or renewed elevations occurred in some older children and adolescents and in selected groups with obesity or severe obesity. Findings by sex and baseline weight status were inconsistent, while socioeconomic and geographic disparities persisted in several settings. Conclusions: Pandemic-associated changes in pediatric weight status partially or completely resolved in some populations but persisted in others. Continued growth monitoring and longer-term, population-representative studies using standardized outcome definitions are needed to identify children with persistent adverse trajectories.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Technologies in Social Science

title: Navigating Higher Education Pre–, During, and Post–COVID-19: Relating Practices to the Interprofessional Education Collaborative Pillars
abstract: Variability in interprofessional education (IPE) has been a documented challenge in health care education prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. The pandemic increased the struggle to implement profession-specific education and IPE, thus requiring shifts in higher education instruction. This study aimed to explore pedagogical shifts focal to the training and application of the Interprofessional Education Collaborative (IPEC) competencies surrounding the COVID-19 pandemic. Qualitative data collection and analysis were employed. Thirty-five months of narrative data collection from 12 National Academies of Practice Speech-Language Pathology Academy subcommittee members followed by online focus groups were employed. The narrative entries were focal to observed or performed IPEC behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic. Analyses utilized sequential coding and interrater agreement followed by an external (non–National Academies of Practice Academy members) interprofessional panel review. Technology, supervision, and accommodations/psychological state were of focus based on the recorded behaviors and events. The IPEC 2016 and 2023 competencies were specifically noted within these three areas. While additional behaviors and events were recorded, comparatively, they were of less focus. IPEC-based pedagogical shifts were identified. Values and Ethics subcompetencies were higher in frequency in both the 2016 and 2023 IPEC versions. Roles and Responsibilities, Communication, and Teams and Teamwork were relatively equal in representation. Future research may be designed to determine how educators increased their communications and collaborations with other health care and non–health care professions.
journal: Perspectives of the ASHA Special Interest Groups

title: Onde a escola está! Uma análise da relação família-escola durante a pandemia de Covid-19 WHERE IS THE SCHOOL? AN ANALYSIS OF THE FAMILY-SCHOOL RELATIONSHIP DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC ¿DÓNDE ESTÃ LA ESCUELA? UN ANÃLISIS DE LA RELACIÓN FAMILIA-ESCUELA DURANTE LA PANDEMIA DE COVID-19 OÃTM EST L'ÉCOLE ? UNE ANALYSE DE LA RELATION FAMILLE-ÉCOLE PENDANT LA PANDÉMIE DE COVID-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic generated substantial impacts on education and on the dynamics of many Brazilian families. This article examines how families with children enrolled in the early years of elementary education coped with the inability to attend school during the period of restrictions on in-person classes, which lasted from March 2020 to February 2022. The study is grounded in the understanding that the school institution plays a multifaceted role within the social structure, going beyond its traditional function of providing formal education. Additionally, the research was conducted under the hypothesis that the impact of school closures on family routines was heterogeneous, varying according to geographic location and the income level of each family. Using a case study approach, this research is based on interviews conducted in areas of the cities of Maringá and Sarandi, adopting a comparative perspective. The results show that schools perform multiple functions. Higher-income families emphasized the impact of the absence of the school environment on their children’s learning and socialization, whereas more vulnerable families missed having a safe, welcoming place that provides basic care—especially with regard to food—thus enabling parents to dedicate themselves to work.

title: Chinese Canadian Youth and Their Experiences with Anti-Asian Attitudes During COVID-19
abstract: The Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has led to anti-Asian attitudes worldwide. Documented discrimination has occurred online and in person. Surveys of Chinese Canadians show a lower reporting rate among youth under 18 than among those aged 18 or older. Chinese Canadian youths’ experiences during COVID-19 remain largely unexplored. This study creates space for their lived experiences and perceptions. Using Interpretive Phenomenological Analysis (IPA), it explores and seeks to understand their perceptions and experiences of anti-Asian attitudes. Six self-identified Chinese Canadian youth aged 16 to 17 from British Columbia's Lower Mainland completed semi-structured interviews on school responses and supports. Analysis followed IPA procedures, identifying three superordinate and eleven subordinate themes. Participants reported anti-Asian attitudes across multiple environments and feeling unsupported in their mental health at school and in the community. Despite limited support, they developed their own support systems. Findings are discussed in relation to existing literature, along with future research directions, school-based practices, and implications for practitioners as reported by participants. The study emphasizes the lived experiences of Chinese Canadians and underscores the importance of addressing anti-Asian attitudes within schools and communities. It also highlights the need to better support Chinese Canadian youth's mental health during the pandemic and beyond based on participant perspectives.

title: Chinese Responses to COVID-19
abstract: Abstract This chapter probes the lessons that China had learned and failed to learn during the COVID-19 pandemic. It begins by examining China’s learning from SARS and explains how SARS became the primary historical analogy for China’s COVID response in the first two months of the pandemic. The chapter then offers a historical analysis of the four phases of China’s pandemic response and identifies what was learned at the end of each phase. It argues that the most important—and problematic—lesson for the Chinese leadership was the Wuhan lockdown and its perceived effectiveness in suppressing virus transmission. Finally, it evaluates Chinese lessons in light of the propositions advanced in Chapter 2 by paying special attention to the Wuhan lockdown lesson and the zero-COVID policy it engendered.

title: Working Remotely from Home During and Post-COVID-19
abstract: Abstract The chapter reviews and analyzes the merits and challenges of people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States regarding working from home in the post-pandemic period when a return to office was mandated by both governments. Both countries had similar legislation regarding reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. The Equality Act 2010 in the United Kingdom was comprehensive, covering disability as one of nine “protected characteristics.” The US ADA Title I focused exclusively on the employment of people with disability. The UK policy showed much more willingness to regulate the labor market during the pandemic and the post-pandemic period and allowed remote working. The US policy demonstrated less interference in the labor market during the pandemic and post-pandemic. The UK government was concerned with employer pushback on remote working and tended to disproportionally affect workers with disability regarding flexible arrangements. The UK policy recognized the right to flexible work, and employees with disabilities still had stronger protection under the “reasonable adjustment” framework. The US federal policy-imposed return-to-office mandate led to a rise in ADA lawsuits regarding the denial of remote work as a reasonable accommodation. The United States carried out the “essesntial functions” test, meaning the key legal question in many US cases was whether remote work eliminated an “essential function” of the job. Although courts aligned with employers vis-à-vis employees’ claims for working remotely, judges in some circuits started considering an employee’s remote work after the pandemic.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: UK and US Policies Regarding Employees with Disabilities During and Post-COVID-19 Pandemic and in a Few Low-Middle-Income-Countries
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, the United Kingdom and United States prioritized flexible working arrangements and adjustments for employees with disabilities, particularly those at higher risk. In the post-pandemic period, both nations have focused on solidifying these flexible arrangements but have also faced criticism over potentially regressive policies related to disability benefits. The UK approach focused on the expansion of access to work. However, the UK government proposed significant welfare reforms aimed at pushing more people into work. The United States prioritized post-pandemic Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) guidance that solidified the legal precedent for remote work as a reasonable accommodation under the ADA. Employers were required to evaluate renewed requests for remote work based on individual circumstances rather than reverting to pre-pandemic policies. Employers were expected to ensure a safe return-to-office (RTO) process but were not required to eliminate essential job functions to accommodate remote work. Finally, case law in the United States continued to evolve regarding what constituted an “undue hardship” for employers denying remote work, often referencing the successful remote work period during the pandemic. The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected employees with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), exacerbating preexisting inequalities in employment, income, and access to services. Post-pandemic policies required a more comprehensive and systematic approach to address the deeper structural barriers to inclusion.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: Impact of Public Health Interventions on the Co-infection Dynamics of COVID-19 with Tuberculosis
abstract: COVID-19 and tuberculosis (TB) co-infection presents a significant public health challenge by increasing disease burden and complicating disease management, diagnosis, and treatment. To explore the COVID-19-TB co-infection dynamics and evaluate interventions such as public health campaigns, mask wearing, and social distancing, we formulate and analyse a novel ten-compartmental deterministic SEIRS model. The model is unique in the sense that it simultaneously includes separate exposed, infectious, and recovered classes for TB, COVID-19 and co-infected individuals, thus providing a detailed description of the disease progression, immunity loss, and co-infection routes. The analysis proceeds by first examining the reduced sub-models corresponding to COVID-19-only and TB-only dynamics, followed by the complete co-infection model. For each case, both local and global stability properties are rigorously investigated using analytical techniques complemented by numerical verification. Model calibration is performed against cumulative weekly COVID-19 case data from Brazil and South Africa to estimate the best-fit model parameters. Numerical simulations reveal that reduction in contact rates substantially decreases the prevalence of both single infections and co-infections. Furthermore, public health campaigns are particularly effective in reducing TB transmission and levels of co-infection, whereas mask wearing and social distancing suppress COVID-19 spread and its associated co-infections. Our results suggest that implementing disease-specific interventions can help reduce the disease burden and offer evidence-based information for the development of effective public health policies in areas where both diseases are endemic.

title: Air Pollution and COVID-19: Impacts on Acute and Long-Term Health Outcomes
abstract: At the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, regional differences in infection rates and disease severity raised questions about the contribution of environmental exposures, particularly air pollution. Early ecological studies suggested associations between long-term exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and adverse COVID-19 outcomes, but individual-level evidence and comprehensive exposome approaches were limited. Moreover, conventional exposure assessment based on residential modelled concentrations may insufficiently capture actual individual exposure, particularly when mobility, indoor time, and pollution patterns change. This thesis integrates epidemiology, biology, and exposure science to investigate how the exposome, particularly air pollution, relates to acute COVID-19 outcomes and post-acute sequelae, while advancing methods for individual-level exposure assessment. A systematic review and meta-analysis (Chapter 2) showed that higher long-term PM2.5 and NO2 exposure was consistently associated with more severe acute COVID-19 outcomes, including hospitalization, ICU admission, and mortality. Although associations were generally smaller in individual-level studies than in early ecological studies, the association between PM2.5 and severe COVID-19 persisted after adjustment for demographic and socioeconomic factors. Chapter 3 provided biological plausibility for these findings: air pollution may induce oxidative stress, persistent inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, thereby increasing host vulnerability and impairing recovery from lung injury. The second part focused on exposure assessment. In Chapter 4, low-cost sensors mounted outside participants’ homes were calibrated and validated against national reference monitoring stations. They showed strong agreement and effectively captured temporal variability and short-term pollution peaks, demonstrating the potential of high-resolution monitoring to complement conventional exposure models. Chapter 5 compared personal PM2.5 measurements with residential outdoor measurements in long COVID patients. The modest correlation and marked discrepancies demonstrated that residential concentrations are an imperfect proxy for individually inhaled exposure. Differences were partly explained by ambient temperature, tobacco smoking, and fireplace use. Chapter 6 examined associations between multiple exposure metrics and objective respiratory outcomes after SARS-CoV-2 infection. While modelled residential exposure showed no clear associations, higher personal PM2.5 exposure was associated with persistent airway abnormalities on chest CT 12–15 months after infection. Individual-level exposure assessment may therefore reveal associations that remain undetected when relying on area-based estimates. Together, these findings suggest that air pollution may influence both acute COVID-19 severity and subsequent respiratory recovery. Importantly, they demonstrate that the selected exposure metric can fundamentally influence epidemiological conclusions. Clinically, environmental exposure information may complement traditional patient characteristics in understanding heterogeneous long COVID trajectories. From a public health perspective, the findings strengthen the case for cleaner air as part of pandemic preparedness: reducing air pollution may lower chronic cardiopulmonary disease burden, vulnerability to severe respiratory infections, and potentially impaired recovery. Future research should embed exposure science prospectively in epidemic-response frameworks through individual-level monitoring, longitudinal clinical cohorts, and infrastructures integrating environmental, clinical, sociodemographic, and biological data. Overall, this thesis provides a framework for exposure-informed precision medicine and demonstrates that accurate assessment of environmental exposures is essential for understanding how the environment shapes susceptibility, disease severity, and recovery during respiratory infectious disease outbreaks.

A systematic review and meta-analysis (Chapter 2) showed that higher long-term PM2.5 and NO2 exposure was consistently associated with more severe acute COVID-19 outcomes, including hospitalization, ICU admission, and mortality. Although associations were generally smaller in individual-level studies than in early ecological studies, the association between PM2.5 and severe COVID-19 persisted after adjustment for demographic and socioeconomic factors. Chapter 3 provided biological plausibility for these findings: air pollution may induce oxidative stress, persistent inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, thereby increasing host vulnerability and impairing recovery from lung injury. The second part focused on exposure assessment. In Chapter 4, low-cost sensors mounted outside participants’ homes were calibrated and validated against national reference monitoring stations. They showed strong agreement and effectively captured temporal variability and short-term pollution peaks, demonstrating the potential of high-resolution monitoring to complement conventional exposure models. Chapter 5 compared personal PM2.5 measurements with residential outdoor measurements in long COVID patients. The modest correlation and marked discrepancies demonstrated that residential concentrations are an imperfect proxy for individually inhaled exposure. Differences were partly explained by ambient temperature, tobacco smoking, and fireplace use. Chapter 6 examined associations between multiple exposure metrics and objective respiratory outcomes after SARS-CoV-2 infection. While modelled residential exposure showed no clear associations, higher personal PM2.5 exposure was associated with persistent airway abnormalities on chest CT 12–15 months after infection. Individual-level exposure assessment may therefore reveal associations that remain undetected when relying on area-based estimates. Together, these findings suggest that air pollution may influence both acute COVID-19 severity and subsequent respiratory recovery. Importantly, they demonstrate that the selected exposure metric can fundamentally influence epidemiological conclusions. Clinically, environmental exposure information may complement traditional patient characteristics in understanding heterogeneous long COVID trajectories. From a public health perspective, the findings strengthen the case for cleaner air as part of pandemic preparedness: reducing air pollution may lower chronic cardiopulmonary disease burden, vulnerability to severe respiratory infections, and potentially impaired recovery. Future research should embed exposure science prospectively in epidemic-response frameworks through individual-level monitoring, longitudinal clinical cohorts, and infrastructures integrating environmental, clinical, sociodemographic, and biological data. Overall, this thesis provides a framework for exposure-informed precision medicine and demonstrates that accurate assessment of environmental exposures is essential for understanding how the environment shapes susceptibility, disease severity, and recovery during respiratory infectious disease outbreaks.

title: Functional Outcomes After Hip Fracture Rehabilitation Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Retrospective Comparative Study
abstract: Objectives: To compare functional recovery during inpatient rehabilitation, assessed by Functional Independence Measure (FIM) gain and FIM efficiency, between the pre-pandemic and COVID-19 pandemic periods in older adults after hip fracture. Methods: This retrospective observational study included patients aged ≥65 years who underwent hip fracture surgery between January 2016 and December 2022 and were admitted to a convalescent rehabilitation ward. Patients were categorized into the pre-pandemic (2016–2019) and pandemic (2020–2022) periods. Functional outcomes included total, motor, and cognitive FIM gain and FIM efficiency. Multiple linear regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with rehabilitation outcomes. Results: A total of 650 patients were analyzed. Admission motor and total FIM scores were significantly lower during the pandemic, whereas cognitive FIM scores were similar between groups. After multivariable adjustment, total FIM gain and total FIM efficiency did not differ significantly between periods. Exploratory analyses showed no significant associations between the pandemic period and motor or cognitive FIM gain or efficiency. Conclusions: Although motor and total FIM scores at admission were lower during the pandemic period, no statistically significant differences in adjusted total FIM gain or total FIM efficiency were observed between the pre-pandemic and pandemic periods.

title: CONDIÇÃO PÓS-COVID-19 (LONG COVID): MECANISMOS INFLAMATÓRIOS, DISFUNÇÃO ENDOTELIAL E PERSISTÊNCIA DE SINTOMAS MULTISSISTÊMICOS POST-COVID-19 CONDITION (LONG COVID): INFLAMMATORY MECHANISMS, ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION, AND PERSISTENCE OF MULTISYSTEM SYMPTOMS CONDICIÓN POST-COVID-19 (COVID PROLONGADO): MECANISMOS INFLAMATORIOS, DISFUNCIÓN ENDOTELIAL Y PERSISTENCIA DE SÍNTOMAS MULTISISTÉMICOS
abstract: A condição pós-COVID-19, também denominada COVID longa ou Long COVID, caracteriza-se pela persistência ou surgimento de manifestações clínicas após a fase aguda da infecção pelo SARS-CoV-2, podendo comprometer diferentes órgãos e sistemas. O objetivo desta revisão foi analisar as evidências contemporâneas sobre os mecanismos inflamatórios, a disfunção endotelial e sua possível relação com a persistência de sintomas multissistêmicos na condição pós-COVID-19. Realizou-se revisão integrativa da literatura, com busca nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science e ScienceDirect, considerando publicações entre setembro de 2021 e setembro de 2026. Foram identificados 731 registros e, após as etapas de triagem e elegibilidade, 14 estudos compuseram a síntese qualitativa final. As evidências demonstram fisiopatologia heterogênea e provavelmente multifatorial, envolvendo ativação imunológica persistente, aumento de mediadores inflamatórios, presença prolongada de componentes virais, alterações do sistema complemento e comprometimento endotelial e microvascular. Estudos clínicos também demonstraram associação entre alterações vasculares e manifestações como fadiga, dor torácica, intolerância ao esforço e comprometimento neurocognitivo. Entretanto, nenhum mecanismo isolado explica todos os fenótipos clínicos. Conclui-se que a condição pós-COVID-19 deve ser compreendida como uma síndrome multissistêmica resultante da interação entre processos imunológicos, vasculares, metabólicos e possivelmente relacionados à persistência viral.
authors: Eberson da Silva Rodrigues Do Nascimento
